text: Everything ArgoCD manages comes down to one custom resource: the Application. It's a small object that answers three questions at once — where does the desired state live, where should it be applied, and how aggressively should ArgoCD keep the two in sync. Once you can read an Application spec fluently, you can read almost anything ArgoCD does.

The source block names a Git repo, a revision — a branch, tag, or commit — and a path inside it, often a Kustomize overlay for one environment. The destination block names the cluster API server and namespace those manifests get applied to. That's the entire model: a desired-state pointer on one side, a target on the other.

Here's the distinction that trips up almost everyone new to ArgoCD: Sync status and Health status are two completely separate questions. Sync status only asks whether the live cluster matches what's in Git — Synced or OutOfSync. Health status asks whether the thing that's running is actually working — Healthy, Progressing, Degraded, and a few others. An application can be Synced and Degraded at the same time: the exact right manifests got applied, and the workload is still crash-looping. Treating Synced as a proxy for working is the mistake to avoid.

By default, ArgoCD only flags drift and waits for a human to run a sync. Turning on automated sync changes that, and two flags control how far it goes. Prune means resources deleted from Git actually get deleted from the cluster, instead of lingering as orphans. SelfHeal means a manual kubectl edit on a live resource gets reverted back to match Git on the next reconciliation loop, rather than just sitting there as flagged drift. Together they're what makes Git the real source of truth, not just a suggestion.

That's ArgoCD's core model: one Application CRD, two independent status dimensions, and a sync policy that decides how automatically Git's word becomes the cluster's reality. Next lesson, you'll see Flux's take on the same GitOps idea — a different toolkit, built from smaller composable pieces: a Source, a Kustomization, and a HelmRelease for chart-based apps.
